name: Wiraféra, Tupí do Machado
confidence_why: No source describes Wiraféd stress at all: the only evidence is Nimuendajú's 1955 wordlist from a single speaker recorded in 1927, whose acute "accento tónico" falls mostly but not always on the last syllable (a-yurú, ae-namí, kwaraí, but óka 'house'), while Pease & Betts 1971, the only phonology of any Kawahib variety, describe the related Parintintin with prominence on the first syllable of the phrase and no word stress, so any placement for Wiraféd is a guess.

new_statements.rule_in_words: NOT a prose rule: the source only defines the acute as the tonic-accent mark and then marks it word by word. In the Wiraféra list the marked accent falls on the last syllable of the word in the great majority of forms (66 of 73 acute-marked forms in the scanned; confirmed on the page scan), i.e. final (oxytone) word stress as in other Tupí-Guaraní/Kawahíb varieties; Nimuendajú 1924 (pp.275-276) and Koch-Grünberg 1932 ('Tupý') mark the same variety the same way. Reading 'fixed: final syllable' is my inference from the marked data.
new_statements.secondary_stress: Nothing; only one accent per form is marked.
new_statements.exceptions: None discussed. In the data a few forms carry a non-final acute (óka 'casa', i-ména 'o marido della', supé-ne, oré-po) and monosyllables/some forms are unmarked.
new_statements.domain_note: Citation forms elicited as a wordlist (isolated nouns with person prefixes, a few short imperative/declarative phrases); word-level marking, no phrase prosody.
new_statements.identity_note: All primary material is 'Tupí do Machado' Kawahíb: Nimuendajú 1955 no.15 is headed 'Wiraféra. Tupí do Machado' (informant from Paraná-sína, right bank of the Machado/Ji-Paraná below Pimenta Bueno, recorded Manaus 1927); Nimuendajú 1924 pp.275-276 'Vocabulario Tupí do Alto Machado' (informant Zacharias Tupy, 1922) is identified as the band 'Wirafed' on Horacio Mangory's word and said to be 'a mesma [lingua] dos Paranawát'; Koch-Grünberg 1932 'Tupý' was taken from that same Horatio Mangurý (born Rio Machado) and is filed by Glottolog under wira1264. Hanke's 'Boca Negra/Dawahib' (1953) is a related but possibly distinct Kawahíb group. The evidence is an accent-marked wordlist, not a descriptive statement; the 'fixed: final syllable' reading is inferred from the marks.

readall_conflicts: No source contradicts another about Wiraféd itself, because no source states a Wiraféd stress rule: the catalog's 'fixed: final syllable' is an inference from Nimuendajú's acute ('accento tónico', 1955 p.150) placed mostly on the last syllable of wordlist forms (1955 pp.175-176; likewise 1924 pp.275-276 and Koch-Grünberg 1932). The one tension is indirect: Pease & Betts 1971, the only phonological description of any Kawahib variety among the listed works, describes Parintintin prominence as phrase stress that 'generally occurs on the first syllable of the phrase' (p.10) and never sets up word stress at all, while Nimuendajú 1948 (p.285) says Parintintin differs from the upper Machado Tupi (Wiraféd) 'only in some phonetic variations'. Different domain (phrase vs word) and different variety, so not a formal contradiction, but it means the Wiraféd 'final' reading has no descriptive-phonology support and should stay flagged as diacritic-inferred.

sources.note: No rule stated. Diacritic key p.150: '´ accento tónico' (+ 'Wiraféra: y inicial tende para dy ou ds'). Vocabulary no.15 'Wiraféra. Tupí do Machado' pp.175-176 marks the acute on nearly every form; of 73 acute-marked forms in the scanned, 66 carry it on the final syllable (a-yurú, ae-namí, apikáb, tanimúk, amán, ibitú, kwaraí, akoimaé, kunyá, kururú..), exceptions óka 'casa', i-ména 'o marido della' and a few phrases; verified on the page scan.

sources.note: 'Tupý' list taken 22 July 1924 in Manaus from Horatio Mangurý, born on the Rio Machado (Glottolog files it under wira1264). 'Character der Sprache' p.31 gives only segmental notes (final b, g very soft; nasalized final vowels; f very soft; w like English wh) — nothing on Betonung. Forms carry acute accents, predominantly final (aeyurú, aerembé, aenamí, aeropá, aerapeyáb, aerameputáb).

sources.citation: Nimuendajú, Curt. 1924. Os Indios Parintintin do Rio Madeira. Journal de la Société des Américanistes 16: 201-278.
sources.note: No rule. '3. Vocabulario Tupí do Alto Machado' pp.275-276 (informant Zacharias Tupy, Manaus Jan 1922; 'Segundo Horacio Mangory este bando é chamado Wirafed'; 'A lingua é a mesma dos Paranawát'). Transcription key p.262 lists special letters only, no accent note; forms are acute-marked, again almost always on the final syllable (ai-namí, ai-robá, kwaraí, maniók, amaniyú, yapasinú, kunumí, yapepoí, igát).
